full_judgment:
2. The relevant fact in short for disposal of this appeal is that the present appellant as plaintiff on 10-6-2009 filed a suit being Title Suit No. 122 of 2009 before the Court of Joint District Judge, 3rd Court, Dhaka for declaration of title in respect of "Ga" schedule property and for further declaration that the sale deed No. 3533 dated 21-9-1997 executed by the defendant No. 2 as attorney of the plaintiff in favour of defendant No. 1 described in schedule 'Gha' of the plaint is fraudulent, illegal, without any consideration and, as such, not binding upon the plaintiff and also for recovery of Khas possession against the present respondent Nos. 1-4 impleading respondent Nos. 1-2 as principal defendants and 3-4 as proforma defendants. The plaintiff case, in short, is that plaintiff Mahbub Ali Khan is exclusive owner of 'Ka' schedule land measuring 13 katha, 5.5. chattack land, who in who in necessity of money for business purpose mortgaged said land with Pubali Bank Ltd. Johnson Road branch, Dhaka against loan money taken by him; subsequently plaintiff, Mahbub Ali Khan failed to repay the loan money and for repayment of said loan, he decided to sell the said land whereon defendant No. 1 proposed to purchase the said land and accordingly the price of the land was fixed at Taka 1,00,00,000 and upon receiving Taka 20,00,000 a baina patra was executed on 19-9-1994 by the plaintiff in favour of defendant No. 1; that in the said baina patra, though the schedule of payment of remaining money was mentioned but defendant No. 1 paid only further 30,00,000 taka to the plaintiff and in such a situation, plaintiff informed the matter to defendant No. 2, full brother of defendant No. Land thereupon, an amicable settlement took place between them upon cancelling the baina patra dated 19-9-1994; that following said settled plaintiff executed and registered a general power of attorney dated 19-3-1997 empowering the defendant No. 2 to construct a multistoried building in the schedule land; that despite the said power of attorney, defendant No. 2 did not construct any building for which plaintiff cancelled the said power of attorney vide another deed of cancellation being No. 4305 dated 8-12-98 and after such cancellation, plaintiff transferred 5 katha land to defendant Nos. 3-4 vide sale deed No. 4339 dated 15-12-98 and delivered possession thereof in favour of them in which being absolute owner in possession of said 5 katha land they after constructed a residential house residing therein; that plaintiff became dumb founded as all on sudden he received notice of title suit No. 437 of 2005 filed by the defendant No. 1 before the Assistant Judge, 1st Court, Dhaka for permanent injunction wherefrom he came to learn that defendant No. 2 in collusion with his full brother, defendant No. 1 has sold out the land of 'gha' schedule vide sale deed No. 3533 dated 21-9-1997 by virtue of power of attorney dated 10-3-1997, in favour of defendant No. 1 though by the said power of attorney defendant No. 2 was not empowered to sell the said land; that in such a position, plaintiff on 31-5-09 requested the defendant No. 1 to deliver the khas possession in favour of him but is of no avail and hence the suit. 

 15. We have heard the learned Advocates of both the sides at length and perused the impugned order dated 18-1-2010 along with other connected papers as filed therewith and also examined the contents of the application for vacating the order of status quo. It appears that the plaintiff-appellant, Mahbub Hossain Khan filed a suit being Title Suit No. 122 of 2009 for declaration of title and recovery of khas possession. After filing of the suit the plaintiff filed an application under Order XXXIX, rules 1 and 2 read with section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure for restraining the defendant Nos. 1 and 3 from continuing the construction work and from disturbing the peaceful possession of the plaintiff in the suit land. The learned trial judge upon hearing the said application by order dated 18-1-2010 rejected the said application on the main ground that the plaintiff could not make out a prima-facie arguable case for getting an ad interim order of junction.
